extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the DOE Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (CSGF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/administrative requirements for applicants to the DOE Computational Science Graduate Fellowship, including who may apply, program-of-study expectations, document submission rules, and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship or residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to apply for the DOE CSGF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants on temporary visas (e.g., F1) are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department teaching/support activity certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Your department must certify that no more than one term of teaching, grading or other departmental support activity is required of you, or that any requirements beyond one term will be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered a DOE CSGF award, your department chairperson will be contacted and required to certify adherence to this DOE CSGF policy ahead of the start of the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time Ph.D. enrollment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a full-time student working toward your Ph.D. at a U.S. university (by fall 2026) in order to be eligible for the DOE CSGF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part-time students are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted academic stage at application
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduate seniors, first-year graduate students and those matriculating into a Ph.D. program (by fall 2026) are eligible for this fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether this applies to you, review DOE CSGF eligibility criteria and additional FAQs or contact the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on prior graduate work
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of application, you cannot have completed more than one year of full-time graduate work toward your Ph.D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who have already completed more than one year of full-time graduate study toward a Ph.D. are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent federal fellowship restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply, but you may have to give up your current fellowship if you receive a DOE CSGF offer. The DOE CSGF cannot be accepted concurrently with another federal fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding another (non-federal) fellowship may be possible but acceptance of DOE CSGF may require relinquishing federal fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of having a master's degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a master's degree does not affect your application to the fellowship as long as you plan to attend a different university for your doctoral studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you earned a master's and plan to enroll at the same university for Ph.D., verify program rules and contact CSGF if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility after time off from school
rubrics_metrics.description: You are eligible as long as you will start a Ph.D. program by the time the fellowship would begin (fall 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking time off to work does not automatically disqualify you if you will start the Ph.D. by the fellowship start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility after master's then work (two-year note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, you are eligible as long as it has been at least two years since you earned your master's degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies a common case where applicants earned a master's and worked before applying; check specific timelines with CSGF if borderline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-of-study eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Students in the physical, engineering, computer, mathematical or life sciences are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you feel your area of study doesn’t fit these categories but does emphasize high-performance computing, the program encourages you to apply and convince reviewers that your work can be properly represented as computational science. Read more about DOE CSGF-supported fields of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-of-study (POS) university eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You can attend any accredited U.S. university offering a Ph.D. during the fellowship period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The POS (Program of Study) requirement must be satisfied for the university you plan to attend during the fellowship; see POS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing university preferences after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If awarded the fellowship, you will be asked to provide a new POS with your selected university that must be approved as a condition of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please contact the DOE CSGF to provide an update to university selections after your application has been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-of-study (POS) review guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally, the graduate advisor at your preferred university will review your POS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this is not feasible, please have your current undergraduate advisor review your proposed POS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application saving and final submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, you can save your application and work on it at any time. Your application is considered final — and no further changes can be made — once you click 'Final Submission' within the 'Review for Final Submission' section of the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can continue using the online system to prompt listed references to submit their letters and/or to check your application’s status after final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and supporting documents deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The application deadline is Thursday, January 15, 2026. Krell Institute will continue to accept reference letters through January 22, 2026 and transcripts until January 31, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log into your application at any time to check the status of received/outstanding documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: For studies beginning in fall 2026, we will notify you by late April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the expected timeframe for award decisions/notifications for the specified cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship start date and renewable term
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship start date will be September 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember, funding is renewable for up to four total years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript requirement (which transcripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: We need an official transcript from every university listed on your application, including the current fall term (if you are enrolled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fall term report isn’t available until after the January 31, 2026 transcript deadline, we will still accept your application and consider it complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript submission methods and delivery rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Official transcripts must be sent directly from the university, either by mail or through an e-transcript system. The latter is preferred when the option exists. Transcripts sent by an applicant will not be accepted regardless of delivery method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All transcripts should be received by Krell no later than January 31, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters requirement and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Your required three letters should be received by Krell no later than Thursday, January 22, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional information on this subject, review the FAQ within the online application system; the applicant may use the online system to prompt references and check receipt status.
